name: API testing automation and Python
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

questions.q: Which decorator defines a reusable pytest fixture?
questions.why: Fixtures are declared with @pytest.fixture.

questions.q: Which decorator runs one test with many input sets?
questions.why: parametrize generates one test per data set.

questions.q: A good negative test for a protected endpoint is:
options: Call it with a valid token and expect 200
Call it with no token and expect 401
Call it with a bigger payload
questions.why: Negative tests check that invalid input is rejected correctly.

questions.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
options: 401: not authenticated; 403: authenticated but not allowed
questions.why: 401 means identify yourself; 403 means you are known but forbidden.

questions.q: With the requests library, how do you read a JSON body?
questions.why: response.json() parses the body.

questions.q: Which approach checks a response structure against a defined schema?
questions.why: Schema validation catches missing fields and wrong types.

questions.q: What does a pytest fixture with scope="session" do?
options: Is created once for the whole test run
questions.why: Use session scope for expensive shared setup such as a login token.

questions.q: Which status code normally means a resource was created?
questions.why: 201 Created. 204 means success with no body.

questions.q: Which HTTP method is NOT idempotent by default?
questions.why: Repeating POST usually creates another resource.

questions.q: What happens with def add(x, items=[]): items.append(x); return items?
options: A fresh list on every call
The same list is reused across calls
questions.why: Default values are evaluated once. Use None and create the list inside.

questions.q: What is an API?
options: A defined way for programs to talk to each other
questions.why: Over HTTP, requests and responses follow a contract.

questions.q: What is a GET request normally used for?
questions.why: GET should not change server state.

questions.q: What is JSON?
options: A text format for structured data
questions.why: Keys and values, arrays and nested objects.

questions.q: What does status 404 mean?
questions.why: The URL or id does not exist.

questions.q: What does status 200 mean?
questions.why: The request succeeded.

questions.q: Where is an API token normally sent?
questions.why: For example Authorization: Bearer <token>.

questions.q: What does the assert statement do in a test?
options: Fails the test if the condition is false
questions.why: pytest shows the evaluated values on failure.

questions.q: In requests, how do you send a JSON body?
questions.why: The json= argument serialises and sets the content type.

questions.q: What is conftest.py for?
options: Shared fixtures and hooks available to tests in that folder tree
questions.why: pytest picks it up automatically.

questions.q: Why pass timeout= to requests calls?
options: Without it a call can hang indefinitely
questions.why: requests has no default timeout.

questions.q: What does response.raise_for_status() do?
options: Raises an exception for 4xx and 5xx responses
questions.why: A quick way to fail fast on error responses.

questions.q: Which marker skips a test with a reason?
questions.why: xfail marks an expected failure instead.

questions.q: In a fixture, what does yield provide?
options: A point to run teardown code after the test
questions.why: Code after yield runs as cleanup.

questions.q: What is a factory fixture?
options: A fixture that returns a function so tests can create several objects
A fixture that builds the server
questions.why: Handy when a test needs many users or records.

questions.q: A flood of requests returns 429. What does it mean?
options: Too many requests; you were rate limited
questions.why: Look for a Retry-After header.

questions.q: Which is a good pagination test?
options: Check first, middle and last pages, page size limits and an out-of-range page
questions.why: Boundary pages are where off-by-one bugs live.

questions.q: Creating a record that already exists with a unique key often returns:
questions.why: 409 signals a state conflict.

questions.q: How do you test your code against a third-party API that you cannot call in CI?
options: Mock the HTTP layer (for example unittest.mock or the responses library)
questions.why: Mocks give repeatable responses, but also add a contract test against the real API sometimes.
